subject: mathematics_2a
question_text: If the letters of the word MASTER are permuted in all possible ways and the words thus formed are arranged in dictionary order, then find the rank of the word MASTER.

mark_split.label: Write the letters in alphabetical order
Count the words that come before
Add up and state the rank

recall_prompt: Say how you would find the dictionary rank of MASTER — what you write first, how you count the words before it, and how you finish.
insider_note: The marks sit in the block table, not in the final addition, and the closing term is +1 for MASTER itself, not a factorial — the words before it count 256, so the rank is one more.

steps.label: Alphabetical order of the letters
steps.margin_note: First mark. Six different letters: A, E, M, R, S, T. No repeats, so every count below is a plain factorial.
lines: Letters of MASTER in alphabetical order:
A, E, M, R, S, T

recall.must_convey: That the letters of MASTER are first written in alphabetical order: A E M R S T.
accept: write the letters in alphabetical order A E M R S T
first arrange the letters of MASTER alphabetically
alphabetical order of the letters is A E M R S T
letters ni alphabetical order lo rayali, A E M R S T
sort the letters first, that is what dictionary order means
heard_as: A E M R S T

steps.why: Dictionary order is alphabetical order applied letter by letter. Until the letters are sorted there is no way to say which words come before the given one.
common_mistakes: Writing the letters in the order of the word (M, A, S, T, E, R) instead of alphabetical order.
Missing a letter — six letters must be listed.

steps.label: Count the words before it
steps.margin_note: Two marks. Words starting with A or E come first (5! each). Then M A E and M A R (3! each), then M A S E and M A S R (2! each). The next word is MASTER itself.
lines: The next word is MASTER itself.

recall.must_convey: That words starting with A and with E are 5! each, then M A E and M A R are 3! each, then M A S E and M A S R are 2! each, and the next word is MASTER.
accept: words starting with A are one twenty, with E one twenty, then M A E six, M A R six, M A S E two, M A S R two and then MASTER
count five factorial for A and for E, three factorial for MAE and MAR, two factorial for MASE and MASR
fix the first letters in turn and count the arrangements of the remaining letters
A tho E tho five factorial, MAE MAR three factorial, MASE MASR two factorial, tharvatha MASTER
one twenty plus one twenty plus six plus six plus two plus two before MASTER

steps.why: Every word that starts with a smaller letter comes before the given word, and once the first letter matches the same argument repeats on the second letter. Each line fixes one more letter and counts the arrangements of the rest.
common_mistakes: Counting words starting with M as a whole block (5!) — M is the first letter of MASTER, so only the M-words before MASTER are counted.
Skipping M A E and going straight to M A S.
Counting M A S T as a block before MASTER — after M A S T only E R remain and MASTER is the first of those two.

steps.label: Add up and state the rank
steps.margin_note: Last mark. 120 + 120 + 6 + 6 + 2 + 2 = 256 words come before MASTER, so its rank is 257.

recall.must_convey: That the counts are added and one is added for the word itself, giving rank 257.
accept: add two forty, twelve, four and one to get two hundred fifty seven
the rank is two fifty seven
two hundred fifty six words come before it so the rank is two fifty seven
anni add chesi plus one cheste two hundred fifty seven
two forty plus twelve plus four plus one is two fifty seven

steps.why: The rank is the position of the word, so it is the number of words before it plus one for the word itself. Forgetting the plus one gives the count of earlier words, not the rank.
common_mistakes: Answering 256 — the count of words before MASTER, not its rank.
Adding 2! for MASTER itself instead of 1.
